concept: One held schematic on a dark bench (your laptop and phone on the left, the site drawn as a door on the right, one line between them) re-runs the same sign-in four times with one change each run: password only, plus a code, a look-alike page relaying both, a passkey that answers only the real address. Lenses and a phone cutaway open the detail that decides each run, a four-cell tally keeps the verdicts side by side, and term cards rise over the dimmed bench between runs without the bench ever leaving. Down is deeper: the evidence sits on a study wall below the bench, and the camera climbs back up to the same exchange for the last practice.

story.arc: the plain exchange and its question; run one, a copy gets in; MFA defined; run two, the copy stops; the meter and its gap; run three, a look-alike page relays both and the viewer predicts; the code and the passkey defined; the passkey signs inside the phone; run four, the passkey refuses the look-alike; down to the evidence; back up, a prompt you did not start is run three seen from your end; the three moves; nothing to hand over

scenes.subject: the sign-in exchange: laptop, phone, line, the site as a door
scenes.accent_on: the password chip, then the code chip, then the opening door

design.treatment: The held picture is built here and not rebuilt until b18: a dark bench schematic, your laptop and phone on the left, the site drawn as a door on the right, one thin line between them. The laptop screen shows a real sign-in page with real words. The sign-in runs once, plainly: a password chip travels the line on 'password', a code chip rises from the phone on 'code' and follows it, the door opens on 'You are in'. Still camera, moving drawing.
design.why_motion: the lesson's object is an exchange over time: what leaves your device, travels, and is accepted. The travel IS the content, and this first run is the baseline every later run is compared against.
elements: laptop: Loom.obj laptop, three-quarter view, screen toward the line, greys (line/muted)

screen: the sign-in page on the laptop screen, every word real: address line 'login.yourwork.example', title 'Sign in', a 'Password' field, a 'Continue' button. Loom.ui has no login artefact yet: build it from Loom.ui.card or ui.doc parts and kit.text, product-neutral (no vendor colour, logo or layout); text at or above the 24 px label floor
phone: upright slab, dark screen that later shows the code '482 913' in mono
line: a thin rail from laptop to door with small direction ticks (world, not counted)
door with door_plate: a tag reading 'login.yourwork.example' in mono (seed label 'tag')
pw_chip ('password') and code_chip ('code'): small ink chips that travel ON the line

beat_sheet.action: the bench is composed from the first frame (never an empty frame): structure settles first, then the line draws from the laptop into the door (about 0.8 s)
dots type into the field at a human pace (Loom interaction typing, 15 to 25 characters a second), then Continue is pressed
leaves the laptop and travels the line to the door, eased, about 1.2 s; accent2 rides on it

beat_sheet.t_anchor: asks for a code from your phone
beat_sheet.action: a short pulse returns along the line to the phone; the phone screen lights with '482 913'; on 'code' a code chip rises from the phone onto the line and follows to the door; accent2 moves to it
the door leaf swings open on its hinge (ease out, 0.6 s, no bounce); a thin pos rim lights the frame; the chips settle into the doorway and fade; the accent leaves

design.continuity: Element names are a contract: the template beats keep and later bespoke beats hold laptop, screen, phone, line, door, door_plate (exact names, created with ctx.el). The chips retire. The door ends OPEN (kept open under the veil in b02 and b03; b04 closes it as run one starts). Geometry: see motifs 'the bench'. b18 rebuilds the same bench at the same coordinates.
design.colour: Colour meanings for the whole lesson: bench structure in line/muted greys; your credentials (password, code) in ink; the threat (copied password, distant laptop, the look-alike box once exposed, the route to them) in accent3; the passkey (sealed key, challenge, signed answer) in accent cyan, only from b13; accent2 warm yellow is the ONE accent, on what the narration names now, and it moves on with the narration. Stamps: ACCEPTED in neg when the thief gets in, DENIED in pos when the thief is stopped; the word carries the meaning, colour repeats it. Technical pack: no overshoot, no stepped time, no boil.

design.treatment: Run one. The bench returns to full value (the veil leaves), the door swings shut to reset, and the run label is stamped into its slot above a four-cell tally. A distant laptop fades in at the top of the free zone, outlined in the threat colour; a copy of the password chip appears on it, travels a second, dashed line that curves down into the door, and the door opens for the copy exactly as it opened for you. ACCEPTED is stamped on the door and in tally cell 1.
design.why_motion: the claim is behavioural: the door cannot tell the copy from you. Only watching the same opening happen for the copy shows it.

scenes.subject: a meter on the door filling to 99.22 percent, with the gap that remains
scenes.accent_on: the meter fill at 99.22, then the unfilled sliver under the lens

design.treatment: The number lives on the furniture: a slim vertical meter is mounted on the door. Instrument law: the track exists with the fill at zero, the fill rises at instrument speed to 99.22 on the spoken number, the reading is marked as it stops, the numeral is named last beside the door. On 'not a guarantee' a magnifier lens opens on the very top of the meter, where the unfilled sliver (0.78 of the track, about 4 px) is too small to read at its real size, and shows it clearly.
design.why_motion: a reduction is a quantity, and its honest limit is a tiny remaining gap. The rising fill carries the size; the lens is the only way to make 0.78 percent of a track visible without changing the meter.

scenes.subject: a phone signing a fresh challenge inside a sealed compartment
scenes.world: inside your phone, through a cutaway
scenes.accent_on: the challenge chip, then the seal on it, then the key that stays

design.treatment: The passkey's mechanism, before the thief returns. The veil lifts. The real sign-in page is back on the laptop with one button, 'Sign in with a passkey'. A challenge chip leaves the door and travels the line to the phone. A cutaway opens a round window in the phone: inside, a sealed key sits in its own compartment. The challenge enters the window, the key presses a seal onto it without moving, and the signed answer travels back to the door, which opens. The key never leaves its compartment.
design.why_motion: 'the secret never leaves' is a statement about movement: everything else travels and the key does not. Only a moving picture can show something staying put while the exchange happens around it.

design.treatment: Run four, the same fake page. The look-alike box splices into the line again exactly as in b08 and the laptop shows the look-alike page with its passkey button. A magnifier opens on the address the request carries, 'login.yourw0rk.example', and marks the one character that differs from the key's own tag, 'login.yourwork.example'. The sealed key in the cutaway stays dark; no answer forms. There is no field to type into, and the box's onward stub to the real door stays empty. DENIED, tally cell 4. design.why_motion: the refusal is an absence: the answer that formed in b13 does not form here. Running the same request and showing nothing travel back is the only way to show an absence.
